speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; can you tell me when these symptoms started and if they occur specifically when you touch the ear canal?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (triggered by mastication) or Cranial Nerve Injury following right tympanoplasty.

Please confirm if you experience any facial numbness or twitching on the affected side, and what specific type of ear dressing or prosthesis you are using now.
